samples.text:
Nowadays, many companies pay famous people on social media, who are called influencers, to advertise their products. There are both advantages and disadvantages of this, but I believe the advantages are greater.

Firstly, this kind of advertising is very effective for companies. Influencers have thousands or even millions of followers, and many of them are young people who do not watch television anymore. So if a company want to reach young customers, it is a good way. Also, it is often cheaper than a TV advert, especially for small businesses. For example, a small clothes shop can pay a local influencer to wear their clothes in a video, and after that the sales can increase quickly.

Secondly, customers can also get benefit. Influencers usually show how a product works in real life, so people can understand it better than in a normal advertisement. They can also find new products which they did not know before.

On the other hand, there are some disadvantages. Sometimes influencers do not say clearly that they are paid, so their followers think it is their honest opinion. This is not fair for the customers. In addition, many followers are teenager, and they can be easily influenced to buy expensive things which they do not really need. Some influencers even promote products that is not safe, for example diet pills.

In conclusion, paying social media users to promote products have some problems, especially when the advertising is not honest. However, I think it is a modern and effective way of marketing that helps both companies and customers, so the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
samples.why: Clear judgement given · relevant ideas with simple examples but limited development · paragraphing present, linking mechanical · adequate vocabulary · several agreement and word-form errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The practice of companies paying popular social media personalities to advertise their goods has grown rapidly in recent years. Although this form of marketing has clear benefits for businesses, I believe that its negative effects on consumers are more significant.

From a commercial point of view, influencer marketing is highly attractive. It enables companies to reach specific groups of consumers, particularly young people who rarely watch television or read magazines. Because followers often feel a personal connection with the influencer, a recommendation from them can seem more trustworthy than a traditional advertisement. For smaller brands, it can also be more affordable than a national advertising campaign, allowing them to compete with larger rivals.

However, it is precisely this sense of trust that makes the practice problematic. Many followers cannot easily tell the difference between a genuine opinion and a paid promotion, especially when the commercial relationship is not clearly disclosed. As a result, consumers may be persuaded to buy products based on what they believe is honest advice, when in fact the influencer has been paid to praise them. This is particularly concerning because many social media users are teenagers, who are more vulnerable to pressure to follow trends. Influencers also tend to present an idealised lifestyle, which can encourage excessive spending and make young people feel dissatisfied with their own appearance or possessions. In some cases, products of poor quality or with unproven health benefits are promoted simply because the influencer was well paid to do so.

In conclusion, paying social media users to promote products is an efficient and relatively cheap marketing tool for companies. Nevertheless, because it often blurs the line between advertising and personal opinion and targets vulnerable young audiences, I believe the disadvantages outweigh the advantages, unless strict rules on transparency is enforced.
samples.why: Clear position throughout · advantages acknowledged and disadvantages well extended, with some generalisation · logical progression · good collocation (blurs the line, idealised lifestyle) · frequent error-free sentences, one agreement slip.

samples.text:
Influencer marketing, in which brands pay popular social media users to feature their products, has become one of the fastest-growing forms of advertising. While it offers undeniable advantages to businesses and, to a lesser extent, to consumers, I would argue that its disadvantages ultimately carry more weight.

The appeal for companies is easy to understand. Influencers command highly engaged audiences, often defined by specific interests such as fitness, gaming or cookery, so a brand can place its message directly in front of the people most likely to buy. This precision makes campaigns more cost-effective than broad television advertising, and it gives small and new businesses a realistic route to visibility. Consumers may benefit too, since a detailed video demonstration can reveal more about how a product performs than a polished thirty-second commercial.

Nevertheless, the model rests on a fundamental tension. Its effectiveness depends on audiences perceiving the influencer as an authentic, independent voice, yet the content is, by definition, paid for. When sponsorship is concealed or disclosed only in small print, followers are effectively misled into treating advertising as personal recommendation. The problem is compounded by the age profile of many audiences: children and teenagers are less equipped to recognise persuasive intent and more susceptible to the carefully curated lifestyles on display, which can fuel both overconsumption and insecurity about body image. Furthermore, because influencers are rewarded for promotion rather than expertise, products such as dubious supplements or risky financial schemes can reach large audiences with little scrutiny.

Admittedly, clearer labelling requirements could reduce some of these harms, but enforcing them across millions of posts remains extremely difficult.

In conclusion, paid promotion on social media is an efficient and accessible marketing channel, yet its reliance on blurring commerce and personal opinion, combined with its reach among young people, means that in my view the disadvantages outweigh the advantages.
samples.why: Sufficiently addresses both sides with a clear, well-argued judgement · ideas logically sequenced and fully extended · cohesion managed skilfully · wide, precise vocabulary (persuasive intent, scrutiny) · wide range of error-free structures.
